title: Nothing checks that the commit a published package pins is one a reader can fetch
foundBy: session agent, from a controlled test in which two agents were each given an installed copy of the package and asked how they would learn to use it
details:
Every documentation pointer in the published package is an absolute URL pinned to the commit the build came from. `scripts/build.mjs` records that commit as whatever `git rev-parse HEAD` returns. Nothing then checks that the commit is one a reader can reach.

So a package staged from a commit that has not been pushed ships with its entire documentation surface dead. That is the README's seven links, the `spec` of all 49 catalog entries, and the manifest's `homepage`. Each returns 404, and nothing in the publish path reports it.

Observed rather than reasoned about. A package was staged from an unmerged branch and given to an agent with no knowledge of this repository. It followed a catalog `spec` to the pinned URL, got 404, then asked the forge directly and was told `No commit found for SHA`. It recovered by reading the default branch instead, which is the outcome the pinning exists to prevent.

The workflows are safe. `npm.yml` runs on a push to the default branch and `release.yml` on a pushed tag, so both pin a commit the forge already has. The exposure is the manual path, which this repository documents: the root manifest's `prepublishOnly` refuses a direct publish and prints `npm run stage && npm publish .package` as the way to do it. Neither half of that command looks at whether the commit is public.

`scripts/stage-package.mjs` already refuses to stage when `dist/BUILD.json` is missing or records no sha. It treats an absent commit as fatal and an unreachable one as fine, and the second ships a package that looks correct and documents nothing.

notes.text: The same check would have to decide what reachable means, and the honest answer is narrow. Asking the forge costs a network call in a script that otherwise needs none. Asking git whether the commit is an ancestor of a tracked remote branch is local and catches the case that actually happens, which is staging from work that has not left the machine.
